title: Observation lab
tagline: Trace the light. Keep the evidence.
failed: The observations could not be opened.
statusDetail: The original frames and quality are available. Source association, motion and photometry have not been validated.
intro: Compare two real SPHEREx exposures of ε Indi B. Inspect their quality and sources, then save your assessment.
emptyDetail: Open the original DR1 and QR3 observations to inspect the images and their quality.
noObservation: No validated comparison is available for this target in this release.
noObservationDetail: Archive inputs may exist. This application has not yet validated their display and quality path; this does not mean the target was unobserved.
contrastNote: Contrast changes the display only. Each frame uses its own percentile stretch.
unregistered: Native cutouts · independently centered · no image registration
blinkWarning: Blinking compares native views. A visual change is not a motion measurement.
countsNote: Flag counts can overlap. SOURCE does not identify the object. OVERFLOW does not mean complete saturation.
quantitativeDetail: Finite values, positive variance and clear flags alone do not establish a reliable detection or flux.
omitted: Prediction omits observer parallax, radial velocity and full covariance. It is not a measured source center.
assessmentHint: What does the image show, what is uncertain, and what evidence supports your judgment?
saveError: Evidence could not be saved. Try again.
restoreSuccess: Evidence restored. Inputs, settings, assessment and result ID match the saved record.
restoreBlocked: This evidence needs recalculation. It has not been restored as a valid result.
invalidFile: The file could not be imported. Use an exported evidence JSON file.
network: The server could not be reached. Check the connection and try again.
noSave: Save this session to enable exports.
pixelHint: Move over an image to read native pixel values.
qualityChecked: Quality reviewed; scientific association remains unverified.
notMeasured: No validated motion or flux measurement
later: Planet X hypotheses, the separate literature distribution and exoplanet experiments are planned next.
ai: AI-assisted application code · Original observations are archival data.
restorePending: Checking schema, input hashes and result integrity…
clearNote: Start a new session after exporting to test restoration.
cancelled: The comparison was cancelled or interrupted. Open it again to retry.
fileLimit: Choose a JSON file smaller than 8 MB.
reviewCount: Review-required pixels are retained for display and counted separately.
hashNote: The saved evidence includes original and calibration hashes, processing version, settings and assessment.
zodiNote: Original L2 IMAGE · ZODI not subtracted · no photometric normalization
searchPlaceholder: Object name · Earth, Pluto, ε Indi B…
universeIntro: Move freely and select an object. Open real observations, inspect quality and sources, and save your assessment.
universeControls: Drag to orbit · Scroll to zoom · Right-drag to pan · Focus the scene for WASD / arrows, Q·E
universeRepresentation: Distances compressed · radii enlarged · map acquisition separate from model time · illustrative starfield
directionDescription: The catalog direction is propagated with proper motion. Observer parallax is omitted. The marker distance is not a physical distance.
solarDescription: JPL ephemeris position at the selected model epoch. The free camera is not an observing instrument.
cameraNotObserver: Camera movement and model time do not change the acquisition time or observer of real exposures.
modelTimeNote: Positions are interpolated between JPL position and velocity samples. Actual SPHEREx acquisition times stay separate in the observation panel.
plutoPredictionNote: The marker is a Horizons prediction for the SPHEREx observer at acquisition time. The observer orbit is TLE-based; this is not a measured centroid or validated motion.
orbitGuideShort: Orbit guides use a fixed reference epoch
orbitGuideNote: The fixed guides are Kepler approximations from JPL osculating elements at the stated reference epoch. They remain fixed during playback and are separate from interpolated body positions or centuries-long integrated trajectories.
orbitExclusions: Nine orbits are shown from Mercury through Pluto. The Sun is the heliocentric origin; no orbit is invented for a stellar direction marker.
playbackEnded: End of supported range · Play restarts from the beginning.
timelineLoadError: Time playback data could not be opened. Try again.
invalidModelTime: Choose a UTC model time within the supported range.
solarInterpolationDescription: This model position is interpolated between JPL position and velocity samples. It is not an original observation or an independent measurement.
exoSurfaceNote: Resolved geographic maps are unavailable for these exoplanets. Terrain, clouds and colors are class-based illustrations, not observed surfaces.
exoOrbitNote: Orbit orientation and current phase are assumed. This system schematic moves with reported periods; it is not a measured current position.
exoScaleNote: Radii and distances are independently exaggerated/compressed for navigation. A 24-hour spin is illustrative. Estimated radii retain their source labels.
exoSkyNote: Catalog RA/Dec are placed on a direction sphere. Pick a point or search the catalog. No distance, 2026 parallax or proper-motion propagation is inferred.
exoLoadError: Could not load the exoplanet catalog.
exoCanvas: Exoplanet direction sphere and illustrative systems. Drag, scroll, or use WASD/QE to explore.
extendedUnavailable: This object is in the catalog. No verified ephemeris supports the current time range, so no position is drawn.
appearanceEpochNote: Maps retain their original acquisition dates. Select a body to load its detailed map. Model time does not create a new photograph.
moonScaleNote: Satellite distances are separately enlarged to avoid overlap with exaggerated planets. Sizes and separations are not to scale; unknown radii use display sizes only.
extendedTraceNote: Additional-body lines show the acquired 72-hour ephemeris interval, not complete orbits or observed motion.
kuiperNote: An illustrative region from 30 to 50 AU. Dots do not represent observed individual positions or density.
galaxyApproxNote: Placed using approximate source directions and distances, with observed morphological features. This is not a precision 3D reconstruction of individual stars or detailed structure.
cosmicApproxNote: Uses an approximate present age of 13.8 Gyr. This conceptual chronology is separate from current ephemerides and actual observation images.
cosmicError: The cosmic chronology could not be loaded.
cosmicVisualNote: The star and galaxy distribution is a synthetic concept illustration, not an arrangement reconstructed from observations.
cosmicControls: Drag to look · Wheel to zoom · WASD to move · Q/E to move down/up
saturnMapGapNote: Black map areas include ring obscuration and missing observations; they do not establish black terrain.
history_description_hot_big_bang: The chronology's reference origin, not a directly observed view of time zero.
history_description_recombination: Represents the approximate milestone when light began travelling freely, about 380,000 years later.
history_description_dark_ages: 10 million years is a display anchor within the broad dark era, not a measured onset.
history_description_first_stars: Theory allows formation as early as about 100 million years; the exact time is unknown.
history_description_early_galaxies: An observed galaxy example at about 280 million years, not the first galaxy's formation time.
history_description_reionization: 500 million years is an anchor within a process spanning roughly 200 million to 1 billion years, not a simultaneous transition.
history_description_galaxy_growth: About 1 billion years is a display anchor for the broad context of galaxy growth.
history_description_cosmic_noon: 2.5 billion years represents the broad star-formation peak around 2 to 3 billion years.
history_description_solar_system: An approximate cosmic age of 9.2 billion years: 13.8 billion minus the Solar System's approximate age of 4.6 billion.
history_description_present: Uses a rounded present-age reference of about 13.8 billion years.
galaxyMorphologyNote: A conceptual model informed by each galaxy’s observed features. Particle counts, detailed arm phase, thickness and display size are illustrative assumptions.
galaxy_shape_inclined_spiral: Inclined spiral disk and dust lanes
galaxy_shape_flocculent_spiral: Fragmented spiral arms and star-forming regions
galaxy_shape_irregular_barred: Irregular structure with a bar and asymmetric arm
galaxy_shape_interacting_pair: Spiral structure interacting with a companion
galaxy_shape_edge_on_dust_disk: Edge-on disk, dust lane and large bulge
galaxy_shape_dust_lane_elliptical: Dust lane across an elliptical stellar distribution
cosmicMorphologyNote: Explore structural diversity in the early universe. Hypothetical galaxies differ in their clumps, compact or elongated structure, small disks or interacting-pair appearance, size, orientation and growth pace.
cosmicMorphologyAssumptions: Shape and growth changes are explanatory models informed by observed examples. Counts, positions, colors, sizes, morphology mixtures and transition times are display assumptions; they do not reconstruct individual galaxies or measured evolutionary fractions.
cosmicMorphologySources: Observed examples · age after the Big Bang
cosmicObsIntro: Explore published observation images and the estimated cosmic ages quoted by their sources.
cosmicObsApproxAge: Estimated cosmic age after the Big Bang
cosmicObsAgeNote: Cosmic ages are approximate source estimates based on redshift and cosmology, separate from image acquisition dates. They apply to the named target or sample, not every foreground or background object in the image.
cosmicObsImageError: The published image could not be loaded.
cosmicObsError: Observation cases could not be loaded.
cosmicObsSlideNote: Play advances observation cases as a slideshow. It does not show physical growth or generate frames between observations.
cosmicObsEnd: Last observation case. Play restarts from the first.
cosmicObs_note_cosmic_gems_clusters: The observation includes different strongly lensed, stretched galaxies and compact star clusters. The arcs in this image are not all duplicate images of one galaxy, and they do not directly give intrinsic 3D shapes.
cosmicObs_note_firefly_sparkle_assembly: Lensing magnifies star-forming regions, with companion objects nearby. These observations alone do not establish this galaxy’s future growth path.
cosmicObs_note_ceers_projected_shapes: The panels show different observed galaxies from a sample spanning about 0.6–6 billion years after the Big Bang. They are not successive frames of one evolving galaxy.
cosmicObs_note_rebels25_rotating_disc: ALMA observations map gas distribution and motion. The colors encode gas signal and velocity, rather than a natural-color optical surface.
cosmicObs_note_zs7_ongoing_merger: JWST observations provide evidence for an interacting system and an ongoing galaxy merger. This is not an image of a future black hole coalescence.
simInputHelp: Enter a date, then press Enter or leave the date fields to apply. The Go button also applies the date.
simNote: JPL long fit · TDB calendar labels · year 0 = 1 BCE. Eight planetary systems only; Earth means the Earth–Moon barycenter. Observation dates stay unchanged.
simInvalid: Enter a valid date within the supported range.
simLoadError: The simulation coefficient sources could not be verified.
simEmbIcon: The Earth globe and map are a representative position marker. They are not the surface or radius of the barycenter itself.
simDescription: A heliocentric position calculated from JPL fitted elements and rates, not a precision ephemeris, observation, or model of billions of years of evolution.
simUnsupported: This long-term model has no state for this object. A position from another epoch is not frozen here.
universeProjectionNote: Markers show published sky coordinates, not a recovered 3D map of depth, physical size or current positions. Drag and scroll to explore; selection zooms in.
universeSymbolNote: Symbols distinguish object types; they are not resolved surface maps or photographs.
universeNucleusNote: This direction references the host galaxy nucleus, not an independent individual black-hole position measurement.
universeCompletenessNote: Explore objects supported by available sources. Galaxy lists are incomplete. Unconfirmed extragalactic planets, unmeasured depth and resolved surfaces are not invented.
universeCatalogError: The hierarchy sources could not be verified.
universeClusterReference: These coordinates reference an embedded cluster, not a measured geometric center of the nebula.
simAccuracyNote: Nominal errors are not guaranteed upper bounds. Do not use this display for precise positioning.
